- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Once the gate allows, both paths merge a `claude/*` head **synchronously** with the REST `PUT repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}/merge` (`merge_method=squash`, `sha=<reviewed head>`) ... never `gh pr merge`" and "the next review run re-checks the gate and merges" (PR DESCRIPTION; also README "one `pulls/{n}` read after a refusal", agents.md "the REST call only merges or refuses", changelog "1 call; 1 `pulls/{n}` read after a refusal", AD-8 "which only merges or refuses")
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh` line 342 and `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` line 2037
  Evidence of absence: Both sites wrap the REST PUT in `gh_retry`. The helper path retries up to 5 times (`gh_helpers.sh:454`, default `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5`); the workflow path retries up to 4 times (inline `gh_retry`, `max=4`). Neither `_is_gh_permanent_failure` (helper) nor the inline version (workflow) marks 405/409 as non-retryable. The implementation does not make a single synchronous merge attempt and defer to the next review run; it retries in-run without re-running the hold gate, recreating the TOCTOU window that the REST call was meant to close. The fix is to replace `gh_retry gh api -X PUT ...` with `gh api -X PUT ...` (no retry wrapper) so a refused merge exits immediately.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Tests cover the synchronous merge in both paths, the lost-response re-read, a merge at another head, and that no claude/* path calls gh pr merge" (PR DESCRIPTION verification table, step 5 evidence)
  Expected change site: `tests/test_claude_merge_hold_gate.py::_run_helper` (line 336) and `tests/test_claude_merge_hold_gate.py::test_deterministic_skip_refused_sync_merge_enrolls_nothing` (line 524)
  Evidence of absence: `_run_helper` sets `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 1, masking production retries and causing the test to pass with exactly one merge call. The deterministic-skip refusal test asserts call shape (`all(merge == SYNC_MERGE for merge in merges)`) rather than count, passing whether 1 or 4 merge calls are made. Neither test verifies that exactly one merge attempt is made on refusal; neither test catches in-run retry behavior. The tests do not verify the documented single-attempt semantics. The tests should assert `len(merges) == 1` and should not suppress the production retry budget in the helper test environment.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
